title: Pluggable batching pipeline and KV windowing refactor to remove global locks
creator: Marcos Rivera
description: Goal: Reduce tail-latency variance and reduce lock contention in the serving runtime by replacing the monolithic batcher/scheduler with a pluggable pipeline and converting the KV cache to a windowed, lock-free read path for hot prefixes. This ticket consolidates several internal tech-debt tasks: removing global batcher locks, introducing per-shard pipeline stages, migrating KV cache accessors to optimistic reads, and applying a minimal dependency upgrade required by the new concurrency primitives. Context: recent p99 regressions under mixed short/long sequences and a spike in mutex contention observed in flamegraphs (see linked dashboard). Approach should preserve current batching heuristics while making the execution path safe for multi-shard worker pools and enabling easier future batching strategies (priority lanes, size-limited windows).
tasks: Design pluggable batching pipeline interface (PipelineStage trait, stage metadata) - RFC
Implement per-shard pipeline runner with bounded queues and backpressure signals
Replace global batcher lock with per-shard epoch token manager
Rework KV cache read path: add windowed snapshot API and optimistic read path for hot prefixes
Upgrade concurrency crate dependency (tokio 1.x -> 1.21) and crossbeam to latest compatible for epoch/atomic helpers
Add unit + integration tests for race conditions and eviction correctness
Performance benchmark harness for mixed seq-length workload and end-to-end latency tests
Rollout plan: feature flag + canary on dedicated pool -> monitor metrics -> flip for all
acceptance_criteria: No global mutex in main batching hot path (verified by code scan and flamegraph)
End-to-end p95 latency <= baseline + 5% and p99 latency reduced by at least 10% on mixed workloads
KV cache hit-rate remains >= baseline for top-100 prefixes and eviction semantics preserved
Automated stress tests reproduce previous contention scenario and show stable throughput
All new code covered by unit tests and integration tests; integration tests run in CI and pass
notes: Key idea: make batching pipeline pluggable so we can later introduce latency-priority lanes without touching core runtime. Use optimistic reads (versioned window snapshots) for hot-key path to avoid locking; fall back to locked path for cold/paged prefixes. Dependency upgrade limited to concurrency crates; coordinate with infra team for glibc/C++ ABI constraints on dedicated nodes.
implementation_strategy: Start with a small RFC to align on API shape. Implement pipeline scaffolding behind a runtime feature flag. Migrate one batcher lane to the new pipeline and run canary traffic on a dedicated pool. Iterate on KV windowing with progressively larger snapshot sizes and benchmarks. Keep a compatibility layer for RPCs between new and old batcher until full rollout.
test_plan: Unit tests for PipelineStage behavior and queue semantics. Fuzzer for race conditions on optimistic reads. Integration test that replays production traces for mixed-length traffic and measures latency and mutex contention. Add CI job to run stress test for 10 minutes with sampling flamegraphs attached to artifacts.
rollback_plan: Feature flag allows turning off the new pipeline; if regressions observed, revert to old batcher by flipping the flag and draining new queues. For KV windowing regressions, switch reads to locked path and run a patch to revert eviction policy change. Monitor canary logs and metrics to decide rollback.
monitoring_and_metrics: Track p50/p95/p99 latency for generation endpoints, mutex contention rate (contention_count), batcher queue lengths by shard, KV cache hit-rate by prefix tier, CPU utilization on worker GPUs/CPUs, and error rate. Create dedicated Grafana panel and alert if p99 > baseline * 1.25 or contention spikes > 3x.
rollout_notes: 1) Merge behind feature-flag. 2) Canary on 5% traffic on dedicated pool with cpu-bound and gpu-bound mixes. 3) Monitor 48h; if stable, increase to 25% then 100%.
